checkpoints: A burst of edits resets the 120 ms timer; no store write occurs before the final quiet interval, and exactly the latest accepted text is written afterward.
A later independent burst saves normally, demonstrating that consumed pending state and timer state were retired.
Empty-string edits save successfully; editing with no current Badge remains a no-op.
Mutating a caller-owned text string after edit acceptance does not alter the text eventually saved.
With pending edits, switching documents, reopening the same document, closing, and disposing preserve the accepted edit under its original document and clean up the departing subscription.
A synchronous navigation initiated by a store listener during a departure-triggered save remains authoritative; the superseded outer open does not install its Badge or document output.
Status events remain filtered to the current document, and different documents retain independent reusable buffers.
Preview still uses its 40 ms trailing interval, emits only its latest query, and hide cancels pending preview work.
After an Action, run the public Ruby syntax check without placing caches or compiled artifacts in the workspace.
forbidden_effects: Do not continue writing document text to the store on every keystroke.
Do not associate delayed text with whichever document happens to be current when the timer fires.
Do not cancel or discard an accepted document edit merely because its Badge is detached, the document is replaced, the workspace closes, or the workspace is disposed.
Do not allow an outer open superseded by synchronous listener navigation to install a stale Badge or publish stale document output.
Do not treat an empty string as absence of pending work.
Do not leak a retired Badge subscription or deliver other documents' status events through it.
Do not change Store event identities, text, revisions, synchronous notification behavior, Workspace/Preview public methods, or document/status payload semantics.
Do not change the search preview delay, coalescing, publication, or hide-cancellation behavior.
Do not edit tests or configuration, and do not place generated binaries, classes, or caches in the submitted workspace.
lifecycle_identity: Each accepted edit belongs to the Badge that was current at acceptance and to that Badge's document-specific BufferBank entry.
BufferBank entries are persistent and reusable per document; Badge retirement ends only the live subscription, not the document buffer or its accepted pending edit.
A pending timer/value pair represents one editing burst. Consumption retires that pair before invoking the callback-capable store write, allowing a reentrant or later edit to form a new burst.
Workspace generation identifies the open or close request that still owns authority to install the next Badge and publish its document.
The departing Badge and buffer must be captured before current ownership is revoked so cleanup and pending persistence apply to the original document.

obligations.text: Workspace#edit must remain a no-op without a current Badge; otherwise it must capture the current Badge's document buffer and enqueue an acceptance-time copy of the supplied text rather than writing immediately.
Each document buffer must use Trailing with a 120 ms delay so repeated edits in one burst reset the timer and only the latest accepted text is written after 120 ms of quiet.
After a burst is consumed, the same document buffer must remain usable and later bursts must schedule and save independently, including an empty-string edit.
BufferBank must continue returning a stable, independent trailing buffer for each document, and its save callback must retain the document identity captured when that buffer was created.

Replacing, closing, or disposing a current Badge must preserve any accepted pending edit. To preserve the former synchronous persistence behavior, retirement must flush the captured departing buffer rather than cancel it, after revoking current ownership and detaching the captured subscription.

Before a trailing task invokes its work callback, it must snapshot the pending value and clear its pending value and handle so synchronous reentry cannot consume the same burst twice and can establish a subsequent burst.

Because Store#write synchronously notifies listeners that may navigate, Workspace#open must revalidate its captured generation after retirement and any departure-triggered save before installing or rendering the requested destination.
Preserve current-document status filtering, subscription cleanup, Store copying/revision/event behavior, document rendering from Store#read, and all existing public interfaces.
Leave Preview unchanged: it remains a separate 40 ms Trailing task whose hide method cancels pending preview work.

ordering_barriers: On edit acceptance: capture the current Badge and its buffer, copy the accepted text, then push it to that captured buffer.
On trailing consumption: cancel the captured handle if present, snapshot the pending value, clear both handle and pending state, then invoke the store-writing callback.
On retirement with a current Badge: capture the Badge, clear @current, detach its subscription, publish the existing document-clear output, then flush its captured buffer before retirement returns.
On open: increment and capture @generation, retire the old Badge, then compare the captured request with the current generation before creating the destination Badge or publishing its document.
Store#write must continue updating the record and revision before synchronously notifying listeners.
preservation: Preserve Workspace methods open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose(), and Preview methods query(text) and hide().
Preserve Store read/write/subscribe/stop behavior, including copied frozen stored text, monotonically increasing revisions, and synchronous notifications.
Preserve document output payloads and reads, status payloads, and filtering status to the Badge's document ID.
Preserve the existing document-clear output during retirement and ensure a superseded open adds no later stale document output.
Preserve independent per-document buffer responsibility and Badge-only subscription responsibility.
Preserve accepted text across navigation and teardown with the same immediately observable persistence availability that the former synchronous edit write supplied.
Preserve Preview's separate 40 ms quiet interval and hide cancellation.

The maintenance change applies to workspace document autosave only.
Store and Preview behavior are preservation constraints, not feature-expansion targets.

Theatre operations — A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval. Document-buffer responsibility: separate BufferBank service
createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide().
Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled.
Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription.
A store listener may call navigation synchronously.
All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.

def initialize(env,id,buffer);@env,@id,@buffer=env,id,buffer;@token=env.store.subscribe {|e| env.output('status',e) if e[:id]==id};end
 def detach;@env.store.stop(@token);end

def initialize(env);@task=Trailing.new(env,40){|q| env.output('preview',{'query'=>q})};end
 def query(text);@task.push(text);end
 def hide;@task.cancel;end

triggers: Workspace#edit(text) while a Badge is current accepts text into that document's editing burst.
A new edit before the existing 120 ms timer fires resets the burst's quiet interval.
A 120 ms timer firing consumes the latest pending document text.
Workspace#open(id), close(), or dispose() retires the current Badge and may encounter pending document work.
Store#write synchronously invokes subscribed listeners, which may call workspace navigation before the outer operation returns.
Preview#query(text) and Preview#hide() continue to trigger only their existing separate transient behavior.
